title: Best Desktop Application Developers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a developer for a Windows, Mac or Linux desktop app: what to include, how to brief it, installers, price factors and red flags.
intro: Desktop applications run directly on Windows, Mac or Linux computers. They suit tools that work offline, handle large files, connect to hardware or need more power than a browser allows. Desktop projects go wrong when the target systems are not agreed, installers and updates are forgotten, or the app is not signed and triggers security warnings. This guide helps you plan a desktop app your users can install and trust.

faq.q: Which operating systems should I support?
faq.a: The ones your users actually use. Supporting Windows, Mac and Linux adds testing and packaging work. Some frameworks build for all three from one codebase; ask the developer about the trade-offs.
Signing the app with a certificate tells the operating system who published it. Unsigned apps often show security warnings or are blocked. Plan for signing certificates in your own name.
Ask for an update mechanism, such as automatic updates or an update check. Without one, users stay on old versions with old bugs.
Say whether the app must work without internet. Offline support affects how data is stored and synced.

faq.q: What should I receive at the end?
faq.a: Source code, build instructions, installers for each system and documentation of any certificates or accounts used.
